name: Wobble box
summary: A turning shaft with an inclined journal nods a trunnioned ring, which rocks an output shaft at right angles to and fro through the journal's angle.

ratio.typical: output swing ±α, the journal's angle to the shaft (±15° here); arm stroke 2 L sin α

topology.notes: ground, input shaft with its inclined journal, the trunnion ring, the output shaft with its yoke; a spherical four-bar, the four revolute axes (input shaft, journal, trunnions, output shaft) meeting at one centre. The kin block keeps the journal sleeve pinned on the input and the arm keyed on the output as bodies of their own (posed with them), so the joint count does not give the mobility: Kutzbach counts 5, which ignores the concurrent axes and counts the sleeve's spin; the true mobility is 1, solved in closed form by the spherical-four-bar block. The loop is overconstrained in the count, as a universal joint is.

explain.motion: The input shaft carries a journal set at a small angle α to its axis, and a ring turns on the journal in bearings. Trunnion pins on the ring, square to the journal, sit in a yoke on an output shaft that stands square to the input. All four axes meet at one centre, so the ring cannot turn with the shaft: it nods, and the yoke rocks the output to and fro through exactly ±α while the input turns on. The swing follows ψ = atan(tan α sin θ), close to a sine, and an arm on the output turns it into a stroke of 2 L sin α.
explain.forces: The input torque reaches the output as a pair of forces on the trunnions, carried by the ring's bearings on the journal. The output moves fastest, at tan α times the input speed, as it passes mid-swing, and its reaction then twists the journal hardest; at the ends of the swing it stands still and a load on the arm cannot turn the input.
explain.benefits: It turns a fast shaft into a strong, smooth, nearly sinusoidal rocking in a compact sealed unit, with only turning bearings and no sliding guides.
explain.limits: The swing is fixed by the journal's angle, so changing the stroke means a new journal. The axes must meet at one point: a machining or shimming error loads the bearings and wears them quickly, and the rocking mass shakes the frame at high speed.

build.ground: base plate with the input shaft's two pillow blocks and the output shaft's, the two axes square and meeting at the centre
build.defining_relations: spherical four-bar with input link α (journal to shaft), coupler 90° (journal to trunnions), output link 90° (trunnions to output shaft), ground 90° (input to output); output angle ψ = atan(tan α sin θ), θ from the pose where the journal leans in the plane of the two shafts (equivalently ψ = atan(tan α cos θ) counted from the pose square to it); amplitude exactly α; output speed ratio dψ/dθ = tan α cos θ / (1 + tan²α sin²θ), at most tan α; arm stroke 2 L sin α
build.notes: Input 360° continuous; the output rocks ±15° at α = 15° and a 60 mm arm sweeps a chord of 31.1 mm. Every axis must pass through the centre. The ring's bearings on the journal take the trunnion loads; the trunnions turn in needle cups in the yoke's arms. At θ = 0 the journal leans in the plane of the two shafts, the trunnions stand upright and the yoke and arm are at mid-swing.

bodies.note: the inclined journal: a sleeve turned at alpha to the shaft, pinned on it

opts.relation: psi = atan(tan(alpha) sin(theta)), the root through the reference pose

review.note: T2 before the build, from the solved kinematics: six phases at 60 degrees of input give swings of 0, -13.1, -13.1, 0, +13.1, +13.1 degrees, so the yoke and the arm visibly rock while the shaft turns; the solve matches psi = atan(tan(alpha) sin(theta)) to 2e-14 at 8, 15 and 25 degrees, amplitude exactly alpha, within 0.13 degrees of a pure sine at 15; the arm tip sweeps 31.1 mm; the output's speed ratio peaks at tan(alpha) at mid-swing; no dwell. Decided: the output shaft lies in plan square to the input, as the universal joint's does, so the two relatives read side by side; the reference pose is mid-swing (journal leaning in the plane of the two shafts, trunnions upright, yoke and arm upright), so the journal angle reads true in PLAN at the start; the journal angle is a control (5 to 25 degrees) with a ghost trace and plot ghosts at 8 and 25, because 'the swing is the journal's angle' is the lesson; the arm's tip is traced with equal-time ticks every 15 degrees (bunched at the ends of the stroke, near harmonic) and a rim point of the ring is traced to show its nod; construction: the four axis lines (input, journal, trunnion, output) and a circle at the common centre, the journal angle arc, the stroke dimension; default view ISOMETRIC, where all four axes and the nod read at once; no section, the principle is in plain view; no use context in the drawing.

claims.text: the yoke rocks the output to and fro through exactly ±α (±15°)
the yoke rocks the output to and fro through exactly ±α (±15°)
an arm 60 mm long sweeps a stroke of 2 L sin α = 31.1 mm
the output moves fastest, at tan α = 0.27 times the input speed, as it passes mid-swing
at 8° the swing is ±8°: the amplitude is always the journal's angle

examples.use: Knife drives on combine and windrower headers
examples.detail: A wobble box at the end of the cutter bar turns a shaft from the header drive into the rapid to-and-fro stroke of the sickle.
Tractor and self-propelled mowers drive their reciprocating knife with a wobble box in place of a pitman crank.
